title: NASA Announces MAX POWER Aerospace Expo and Airshow at Kennedy Space Center
excerpt: The agency's newest public event will feature Artemis astronauts, Air Force Thunderbirds, and hands-on aerospace experiences as part of celebrations marking America's 250th anniversary.
body:
• NASA has announced MAX POWER, a new aerospace expo and airshow to be held at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
  • The event will feature Artemis moon mission astronauts, the Air Force Thunderbirds demonstration team, and interactive aerospace exhibits.
  • MAX POWER is part of celebrations marking the United States' 250th anniversary, or semiquincentennial.
  • The expo aims to inspire a new generation of aerospace professionals and showcase America's space and aviation capabilities.

NASA has unveiled plans for MAX POWER, a major new aerospace expo and airshow set to take place at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, combining cutting-edge space technology demonstrations with aerial performances in what the agency bills as a celebration of American innovation.

The event, announced this week, will feature appearances by Artemis program astronauts who are preparing for humanity's return to the Moon, along with a performance by the Air Force Thunderbirds aerial demonstration squadron. NASA has promised attendees the chance to "strap yourself in and feel the Gs" through immersive experiences and hands-on exhibits.

Marking 250 Years

MAX POWER is being organized as part of the broader national celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of the United States in 2026. By staging the event at Kennedy Space Center — the historic launch site for the Apollo missions and the Space Shuttle program — NASA is drawing a direct line from the nation's founding ideals to its ambitions in space.

https://x.com/NASA/status/2088355206723477740

The expo will showcase both NASA's current programs and its future plans, including the Artemis campaign to establish a sustained human presence on and around the Moon, and early-stage planning for crewed missions to Mars.

Aviation Meets Space

In addition to space exhibits, MAX POWER will feature a full airshow component. The Air Force Thunderbirds — the U.S. Air Force's premier aerial demonstration team — will perform their high-speed precision routines, while static displays will include both military and civilian aircraft spanning decades of American aviation history.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=b53je_sdlDU

Aviation Week reported that the expo will also feature demonstrations from commercial space companies, reflecting the growing role of the private sector in America's space enterprise.

Inspiring the Next Generation

NASA has positioned MAX POWER as more than an airshow — it is part of the agency's broader push to recruit and inspire the next generation of aerospace engineers, scientists, and astronauts. The event comes as the U.S. faces a growing need for STEM talent in both its civilian and defense aerospace sectors.

For Indian American families, the event offers an opportunity to engage with NASA's work firsthand. Indian Americans have played increasingly prominent roles at NASA, from astronaut Sunita Williams to numerous engineers and scientists leading key programs across the agency.

What's Next

NASA is expected to release detailed scheduling and ticketing information in the coming weeks. Kennedy Space Center, located on Florida's Space Coast, draws millions of visitors annually through its visitor complex, and MAX POWER is expected to be one of the signature public events of America's 250th anniversary celebrations.
